title: 4 devs, no designer, almost a year in: what AI actually did (and didn't do) for our multiplayer tactics game
author: NicoBacc
selftext:
Quick context first: we're a team of 4 developers plus a tester. Nobody on the team is a game designer or an artist. I've been doing apps and websites for about 10 years, and my only previous game was a multiplayer racing game in Unity that I eventually shut down when the players stopped showing up.  
So when we started Vaelix almost a year ago, the obvious question was how we were going to cover everything we don't know how to do. Short answer: a lot of AI, but not in the way I expected at the start.

**Design.** We used ChatGPT mostly as a sparring partner. Not "design me a game", more like throwing ideas at it and having it poke holes in them. The core idea came out of that: 3v3, both players plan at the same time, everything resolves together. No turns, no waiting.

**Code.** The first implementation went through OpenCode, mostly with DeepSeek V4.1 and GLM 5.3. Fast for getting things up and running, but it piles up assumptions you don't notice until later. Lately we've been using Claude for the opposite job: reading through the code, finding edge cases, questioning decisions. Less exciting, honestly more valuable at this stage.

**Art and audio.** This is where it made the biggest difference for us, since we had literally nobody for it. Characters, UI and sounds all started from AI-generated material, but almost nothing went into the game as-is. Lots of iteration, and lots of "no, this looks like a SaaS dashboard, it needs to look like a game".  
**What AI couldn't do for us:** playtesting. The most interesting stuff only came out of real matches. With simultaneous moves, heroes that pull enemies, teleport, protect teammates or rewind someone to an earlier position combine in ways we never planned. And we only added the Collapse mechanic (the arena shrinks over time) after realizing that people could just play defensively forever. No model told us that, our tester did 😅

Stack is Flutter + Firebase. Not the obvious pick for a real-time multiplayer game, but it's what we know best, and so far it's held up better than I expected.  
We're in the final testing/polishing phase now, aiming for a November release on iOS and Android. The video shows where the game is today.

Curious to hear from people here who went the same route: where did AI save you the most time, and where did it end up costing you time instead?

Waitlist if you want to follow along: [https://vaelix.app](https://vaelix.app/)

comments.author: ripple182
comments.body: How painful was it to get the 2d sprite animations to be consistent by using AI to generate them?  I could not get a handle on it and moved towards 3d models in blender to maintain consistency.
